The claim makes two assertions about Intel's Q3 2026 performance: (1) gross margin improved, and (2) total revenue declined.

GROSS MARGIN IMPROVEMENT - SUPPORTED:
The evidence clearly establishes that gross margin improved in Q3 2026 compared to Q3 2025. E11 shows gross margin increased from 38.2% to 43.0%, a 4.8 percentage point improvement. E2 confirms consolidated gross profit increased by $1.9 billion or 36% in Q3 2026 vs Q3 2025. The computed figures from E7 and E8 show Q3 2026 gross profit of $7,096M on revenue of $16,513M, yielding a 43.0% margin, compared to Q3 2025's 38.2% margin.

TOTAL REVENUE DECLINED - CONTRADICTED:
The evidence definitively contradicts the claim that total revenue declined. E12 shows consolidated revenue increased from $13,653M in Q3 2025 to $16,513M in Q3 2026, a 20.9% increase. E3 corroborates this, stating "Total Intel Products revenue was $15.4 billion in Q3 2026, up $2.8 billion from Q3 2025."

H1 challenged whether consolidated revenue actually declined despite segment revenue increases - this is REFUTED by E12 and E14 showing total revenue increased.

H2 explored whether the claim might refer to sequential (Q2 to Q3 2026) decline - the evidence retrieved (E16, E17) discusses Q2 2026 but does not provide a Q3 2026 vs Q2 2026 comparison, so NO_RELEVANT_EVIDENCE.

H3 challenged whether margin percentage actually improved or just gross profit dollars - this is REFUTED by E11 showing margin percentage definitively increased from 38.2% to 43.0%.

Since one material part of the claim (revenue declined) is contradicted by the evidence, the verdict remains CONTRADICTED.
